description.en: A short sample e-book on Assamese literature — from the early Charyapada and Vaishnavite works to the modern Jonaki era and contemporary writers. Full chapter content will be added soon.
description.as: অসমীয়া সাহিত্যৰ ওপৰত এটা চমু নমুনা ই-বুক — আদিম চৰ্যাপদ আৰু বৈষ্ণৱ যুগৰ ৰচনাৰ পৰা আধুনিক জোনাকী যুগ আৰু সমসাময়িক সাহিত্যিকলৈ। সম্পূৰ্ণ অধ্যায়ৰ বিষয়বস্তু অচিৰেই যোগ হ'ব।

content.en:
The earliest specimen of Assamese literature is found in the Charyapada, a collection of mystic Buddhist songs written around the 8th to 12th centuries. The first great Assamese poet was Madhav Kandali, whose Saptakanda Ramayana translated the Ramayana into Assamese.

The Vaishnavite period, led by Srimanta Sankardeva and his disciple Madhavdeva, marks the golden age of Assamese literature. Sankardeva composed the Kirtan Ghosha and wrote Ankiya Naat plays, while Madhavdeva composed the famous Namghosha. Their works used simple language to spread devotion and are still recited in Namghars across Assam.

Modern Assamese literature began with the missionary era and the publication of the Arunodoi magazine in 1846. Anandaram Dhekial Phukan was a pioneer of modern Assamese prose. In 1890 Padmanath Gohain Baruah wrote Bhanumati, the first Assamese novel, and later founded the Asam Sahitya Sabha.

The Jonaki era (1889 onwards) produced the greatest modern Assamese writer, Lakshminath Bezbaroa, known for his humorous essays and the folk tale collection Burhi Aair Sadhu. In the twentieth century, Jyoti Prasad Agarwala and Bishnu Prasad Rabha enriched Assamese literature, drama and music, and modern writers continue to build on this rich heritage.
